items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name — zero name uses across the entire call
No 'How are you today?' or any personal check-in at the open
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight into confirming square footage after the audio check
Never confirmed origin/destination addresses or zip codes out loud; read parking and stairs off the file ('I'm not seeing any issues with parking on either end, no stairs') instead of asking
Never probed additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony), special considerations (long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns), or access concerns
Never asked about packing needs
Never asked the moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
'Everything is included within that hourly rate' — never itemized gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools
Disassembly/reassembly never mentioned despite an IKEA bed, a 22-piece sectional, and multiple Kallax shelving units
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned
Meet Your Mover never pitched
On-Time Guarantee never pitched — gave arrival windows but no guarantee
'No additional fees, cost or charges' stated generically; never ran the itemized no-hidden-fees pitch (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees)
Number of trucks never stated (only 'two movers')
No estimate variables explained — nothing on the 8 dirt-filled pots, the 30–40 heavy pavers, walk distance from a muddy backyard, or disassembly time, all of which are the actual drivers on this job
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped on a move happening the very next morning
'No deposit required' never mentioned
Never described the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked the customer to reply with corrections
Business hours never given
No insurance explanation at all (No Worries + 60¢/lb baseline)
top_strength: The inventory intake was genuinely thorough for an unusual partial-load job — he patiently walked the customer through bed, sectional, shelving units, pots, pavers and lawn items, pinning down counts and rough dimensions on the pavers rather than accepting 'a bunch.' He also handled the customer's text-instead-of-call request immediately and confirmed he'd note it.
coaching_note: This move was booked for the next morning with 8 dirt-filled pots, 30–40 heavy pavers, and loose lawn items sitting in a muddy backyard — the single highest-value thing Garrison could have said, and did not say at all, was the Save Your Ass prep speech. Ten seconds of 'anything small and loose you can consolidate or take a carload of tonight comes straight off tomorrow's bill' would have cut real time off a job he estimated at 3–4 hours. Pair that with tying the estimate to those specific items (pavers, pots, walk distance, disassembly on the sectional) instead of a bare '3 to 4 hours,' so the customer understands what actually moves the number.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and accommodating with steady affirmations, but the warmth is filler-driven ('okay, perfect,' 'alrighty, fantastic' repeated throughout) rather than personal — he never used the customer's name once and built no rapport beyond the transaction.
